newsitem.title: USA: U.S. West Coast crudes fall with players sidelined.
newsitem.headline: U.S. West Coast crudes fall with players sidelined.

text.p: U.S. West Coast crude prices fell in lackluster Friday trade, with players stepping out of the market to evaluate next month's supply needs traders said.
The region's main Alaska North Slope (ANS) seller declined to give a price until buyers stepped forward.
ANS remained available for April delivery peged off spot April West Texas Intermediate (WTI), the seller said.
"More than likely we'd sell (barrels) off May and capture the roll," he added.
BP on Thursday sold 100,000 barrels of Alaska North Slope (ANS) to a small West Coast refiner for -$0.85 off WTI, traders said.
The shipment was too small to influence overall discounts, which remain -$0.91 off WTI. ANS was talked $20.69/20.89 a barrel, off 30 cents a barrel.
Other light grades were unchanged, with Line 63 prices holding at postings plus $0.95 to $1.00.
Outright prices for Kern River remained steady for the third-straight day. Kern River, a key heavy grade, ranged $13.53/13.63 a barrel.
